thread:
marc: Heads-up — scheduling a canary for Maeve (tenant: maeve-prod) on Dedicated. Need ops + release signoff. Window: 2026-03-22 02:00–04:00 UTC. Canaries: 5% -> 25% over 45m. Target image: rwinf/v1.4.2-dedicated-2026-03-22.

sasha: noted. are we pinning the model binary and quantization profile for the canary?

marc: yes — pinning to model: redwood/llm-x-6b@sha256:0a1b... and qprofile: qp-8bit-faster. Deploy config in the runbook link below.

deploy-bot: [deploy scheduled] Canary start scheduled by @marc at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z. Playbook: https://runbooks.redwood/maeve-dedicated-canary.

anya: quick check — latency SLO for this tenant is 120ms p95. What's our acceptance threshold?

jo_release: acceptance: p95 < 180ms and error rate < 0.5% during canary stages. If p95 > 250ms OR error rate > 1% for 5m -> auto-rollback. Manual rollback if any customer-facing regressions reported.

liz_ops: adding infra constraints — we need to reserve the dedicated slice and set autoscale min to 2 GPUs for the canary slice. Also KMS rotation is in progress in eu-west-1 earlier that day; confirm region mapping.

marc: thanks Liz — canary will be in us-west-2 only to avoid the KM rotation window. Reserved slice: maeve-dedicated-canary-02. Autoscale min=2, max=6.

anya: noted. Does the rollout include the new KV cache optimization? That one changed cache eviction at startup.

marc: yes, it's enabled behind flag kvcache.v2=true for the canary only. We have smoke scripts in the runbook to validate cold-start behavior.

deploy-bot: [preflight checks] config lint OK, image rwinf/v1.4.2-dedicated-2026-03-22 verified, slice reservation OK.

jo_release: release notes summary posted: https://releases.redwood/maeve/1.4.2 — include fallback plan and eval set. Everyone ack?

sasha: ack from ML side. I've run the eval set, no quality regressions on the prompt suite used by Maeve.

liz_ops: ack from infra. slice reserved and network policies applied. I set a 30-minute alert for any memory growth > 85%.

anya: ack from platform. KV cache smoke passed locally. I'll be on-call during window.

marc: thanks. final question — do we want to run a small canary at 1% for 10m first, then 5% -> 25%?

jo_release: yes, do the 1% verifier for 10m. If all green, proceed to 5% for 15m, then 25% for 20m.

deploy-bot: [timeline] 02:00 UTC -> 1% verifier (10m); 02:10 -> 5% stage (15m); 02:25 -> 25% stage (20m); 02:45 -> monitor hold (15m). Auto-rollback policy active.

marc: perfect. tagging on-call: @anya @liz_ops. Please react in-thread with :thumbsup: if you approve.

anya: :thumbsup:

liz_ops: :thumbsup:

jo_release: :thumbsup: — documenting rollback rationale: immediate rollback if error spikes or model quality metrics drop beyond tolerances; otherwise follow staged rollback if persistent.

sasha: leaving a quick command snippet for rollback lock if needed:
```bash
# pin tenant back to previous image
redwoodctl tenant pin --tenant maeve-prod --image rwinf/v1.4.1-dedicated-2026-03-10
# notify on-call
redwoodctl notify --team ops --msg "Maeve canary rollback: pinned to v1.4.1"
```

marc: adding a final note: make sure the telemetry tag 'canary_maeve_v1.4.2' is included so we can filter metrics quickly.

deploy-bot: [deploy queued] Canary queued at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z. Operators: @anya, @liz_ops. If anything changes ping #eng-oncall.

marc: thanks team — I'll kick off the canary at the window unless anyone DM's objections.

liz_ops: I'll be on standby in case we need to cut traffic or throttle slices.

anya: I'll run the smoke checks and watch the eval dashboards. Good luck.

jo_release: leaving final release note comment: document the canary outcome and any cherry-picks to the release branch by EOD.

marc: confirmed. closing thread; will post outcome after the window.
